title: Power Automate process mining: Process Intelligence Studio for object-centric models
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the table incorrectly says automation for restricting capacity allocation is undocumented, although Microsoft documents the tenant setting and its PowerShell management. The capacity allocation path omits a required tab on its cited page, and the API entry is an operation-family label rather than a usable call. The planned OCPM workspace also needs distinguishing from the more limited preview Microsoft currently documents.

claims.claim: Process Intelligence Studio is a customisable analysis workspace in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining. It delivers a comprehensive, customizable dashboard for exploring process intelligence insights.

claims.claim: The workspace offers tab-based navigation.
claims.quote: Multiple tabs for organizing different analytical perspectives

claims.claim: Tiles or cards can be arranged in flexible grid layouts.
claims.quote: The main canvas displays multiple cards arranged in a grid layout.

claims.claim: The planned workspace supports filters applied once that cascade across its tiles.
claims.quote: Unified filtering: Apply filters once and have them cascade across all tiles in your workspace

claims.where: What's changing; Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Workspace configurations can be saved and reused as analysis templates.
claims.quote: Process Intelligence Studio saves your workspace configurations, allowing teams to create reusable analysis templates

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Change & support
claims.claim: Dashboard configurations or views can be shared with colleagues.
claims.quote: Collaboration: Share specific tabs or entire dashboard configurations with team members.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The item extends the full workspace to OCPM models alongside traditional case-centric models.
claims.quote: Object-centric support: Extends full functionality to OCPM models, enabling multi-dimensional analysis of interconnected objects, relationships, and cross-object metrics within the same intuitive interface.
claims.fix: Attribute full workspace parity explicitly to the roadmap plan, rather than describing it as current OCPM behaviour. Add that https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/object-centric-process-overview currently documents an OCPM preview with only the Process overview tab and Default view.

claims.claim: One OCPM event can relate to several objects, including orders, invoices and payments.
claims.quote: OCPM lets one event belong to multiple objects (and object types), keeping the full context intact.

claims.claim: OCPM models are built by ingesting an object-centric event log stored in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.
claims.quote: To access OCPM (object-centric process mining) in Power Automate Process Mining, first create a process model by ingesting the object-centric event log (OCEL).
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/object-centric-ingest-event-log to sources; it explicitly instructs storing the event log in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake, whereas the cited conceptual overview does not.

claims.claim: Learn calls the interface the process intelligence experience.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to process mining follows environment and process security permissions.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: The event log's storage location introduces access prerequisites.
claims.quote: The Owner role (on a storage account level) must be attributed to the user performing the initial container setup (user then becomes the Owner of the process).
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/process-mining-byo-azure-data-lake and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/process-mining-files-fabric-onelake for storage-specific prerequisites. Clarify that these are connection/setup permissions, not a claim that every report viewer needs direct storage access.

claims.claim: Event logs can contain order and invoice identifiers.
claims.quote: each row is an event (with activity and timestamp) and has one or more columns listing the object IDs per object type that the event touched (for example, Order=O2, Invoice=I1).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Environment Maker role can create processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is analysis only and introduces no external actions.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience actions analysis. Opened process-mining-studio-overview and object-centric-process-overview; they describe analytical functionality but do not expressly establish the blanket absence of external actions.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical absence with 'The roadmap describes an analysis workspace, not a new autonomous automation capability.' Keep the low-risk assessment as the wiki's judgement rather than an exhaustive product guarantee.

claims.claim: Process mining has documented licensing within Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate. Three Power Automate licenses relate to process mining

claims.claim: Azure Data Lake storage carries storage costs.
claims.quote: Azure Data Lake Storage is priced at Azure Blob Storage levels.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-introduction for the Azure Data Lake storage-cost statement.

claims.claim: OneLake storage carries storage costs.
claims.quote: As you move from the hot tier to the cool or cold tier, static storage prices lower but transaction prices rise.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/onelake/onelake-storage-tiers for the OneLake storage-cost statement.

claims.claim: Power Automate Premium licences contribute process mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on contributes additional process mining capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool, which users with the Power Automate Premium license can use.

claims.claim: Process mining capacity is pooled tenant-wide.
claims.quote: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.claim: Process mining storage capacity can be allocated per environment.
claims.quote: Allocate and deallocate the currencies for the environment. ... ExternalCurrencyType ... ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: The cited allocation page gives Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Add-ons > Manage.
claims.quote: On the Capacity page, select the Summary tab. ... Scroll down to the Add-ons section, and select Manage.
claims.fix: Use 'Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Summary > Add-ons > Manage' for this docs URL. The separately linked programmability tutorial gives the older Add-ons tab > Manage route; mention that documentation difference rather than silently mixing the paths.

claims.claim: 'Currency allocation operations (Power Platform licensing API)' supplies the API call for changing process mining allocations.
claims.quote: Searched: Process mining capacity environment allocate. Opened currency-allocation and its Get/Patch references. The printed text is an operation-family description, not a call with an HTTP method, path, API version or allocation body.
claims.fix: Replace the label with 'PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01' and document body {"currencyAllocations":[{"currencyType":"ProcessMiningDataStorage","allocated":<count>}]}. Set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-platform/licensing/currency-allocation/patch-currency-allocation-by-environment.

claims.claim: Capacity allocation permissions can be restricted at Settings > Power Platform settings > Tenant settings > Add-on capacity assignments > Only specific admins.
claims.quote: In the title bar, select the Settings icon. ... Select Power Platform settings. ... On the Tenant settings page, select Add-on capacity assignments, and then select Only specific admins.

claims.claim: Automation for restricting who may allocate add-on capacity is not documented.
claims.quote: disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins | Boolean | Ability to disable capacity allocation by environment administrators. Default value is false.
claims.fix: Replace null with PowerShell management using Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody @{disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins=$true}. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/set-tenantsettings and the setting definition at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/list-tenantsettings; flag the latter documentation as preview.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No dedicated UI or API switch for Process Intelligence Studio or object-centric models is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Process Intelligence Studio object centric enable disable admin setting API; object-centric process mining disable API. Opened studio overview, OCPM overview, OCPM ingestion, security and list-tenantsettings; no dedicated switch found.

claims.claim: The allocating-add-ons tutorial shows allocation through a Power Automate flow.
claims.quote: Allocate an add-on using Power Automate flows or Logic Apps ... Add a new action to the canvas, searching for "Allocate and deallocate the currencies for the environment".

claims.claim: The checklist's controls for Environment Maker assignment and sensitive process access are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Check who holds the Environment Maker role. ... Review who can see sensitive process data. ... Controls rows: capacity allocation, capacity allocators, and a missing feature switch.
claims.fix: Add controls rows for environment security-role assignments and process sharing/access, using the documented process mining security model. The note on the absent feature switch is not a row explaining either access control.

claims.claim: An automatically enabled change for process analysts and owners has low impact because most users never see it.
claims.quote: impact: low ... Low. Process analysts and owners use it; most users never see it.
claims.fix: Set impact to medium and explain that it affects specific analyst and process-owner roles. The scale reserves low for admins only or a small opt-in group; the record says this change is enabled automatically.
